Featured stories

Each month our pānui (newsletter) includes a feature story from a participant in Wai Tuwhera o te Taiao. We also showcase a species found in eDNA samples.

Check out our pānui / newsletter

Read past issues and subscribe

Read the full feature story

Locals rally for native planting day

EcoMatters Environment Trust in Auckland has been harnessing the power of eDNA to activate their community, using their testing results to help secure funding for their recent native planting drive. Pamela Gill, the trust’s Principal Advisor Restoration, Community and Iwi Relationships, talks to us about how eDNA is a great tool for helping tell the story of their local waterways.

 

Find out more about the kākahi

Species spotlight for June/Hune

There are three species of kākahi / freshwater mussels found only in the rivers and lakes of Aotearoa New Zealand.

Kākahi are classed as at risk due to their small, declining population. They reproduce slowly and rely on native fish such as kōaro (climbing galaxias) to carry their larvae upstream to grow. A source of kai for iwi and hapū, sadly some kākahi may not be safe to eat due to river pollution.

Read the full feature story

Community Group Spotlight: Barkers Creek Catchment Group

Farmers in a South Canterbury catchment group are drawing on a raft of innovative ideas – from DNA testing to the humble dung beetle - to help improve their local waterways.

Find out more about the pied shag

Species spotlight for Āperira/April

Classed as nationally vulnerable, the kāruhiruhi (pied shag) is only found in Aotearoa New Zealand and Australia. Despite spending a lot of their time near the sea, their feathers are not waterproof, and they are often seen drying them out so they don’t get cold or weighed down. They get their name from their distinctive white belly and black backs.

Read the full feature story

Community Group Spotlight: Friends of Awa Matakanakana (FOAM) 

Discovering there could be an important endemic species in your neighbourhood, is not just interesting – it’s inspirational. When the 2023 eDNA results came back to Friends of Awa Matakanakana (FOAM) volunteers, they were intrigued to see there was a small hit for giant kōkopu in the catchment north of Auckland.

Read the full story

Community Group Spotlight: Bay Conservation Alliance

The Bay Conservation Alliance cadet programme helps people to upskill by teaching them how to use a range of monitoring tools, including eDNA testing. Cadet Training Manager Emma Richardson explains how these skills are helping cadets find jobs protecting te taiao.

Find out more about the īnanga

Species spotlight for Pēpuere/February

Īnanga, or the common galaxias Galaxias maculatus, is one of the five native species of whitebait found in Aotearoa. This native species is also found in other places in the Southern Hemisphere. Īnanga are a taonga species and are an important mahinga kai (food source) for iwi, hapū and whānau around the motu. 

Read the full feature story

eDNA testing helps reveal cyclone's effect on waterways

Cyclone Gabrielle wrought devastation across Hawke’s Bay and Tairāwhiti. One year on, we are supporting the community to use cutting-edge DNA technology to help reveal the cyclone’s effect on the region’s waterways.

Read the full feature story

Elusive animals detected in Southland/Murihiku restoration area

Environmental DNA (eDNA) testing has revealed the presence of several threatened and elusive native species within a traditional Māori food and resource gathering (mahika kai) restoration area.

Find out more about the longfin eel

Species spotlight for Noema/November

During the day the ōrea, or longfin eel, rests. Anguilla dieffenbachiai stays secretive and hidden, resting underwater in the cool shadows of plants and trees, or under rocks or logs. Once day turns to night, the ōrea ventures out to search for small fish and insects to eat, cloaked in the darkness. The longfin eel is one of two main species of tuna, or eel, found in Aotearoa and the only endemic species.

 

Read the update

Community Group Spotlight: Ahuriri Tributaries Catchment Group Trust

The Ahuriri Tributaries Catchment Group Trust share an update on their mahi, plans for the future and recent community seminar. 

Find out more about the spiny gilled mayfly

Species spotlight for Mahuru/September

The spiny gilled mayfly, or Coloburiscus humeralis, is a species of piriwai found only in Aotearoa New Zealand. Piriwai are sensitive species which means they can only survive and thrive in clean water, so the presence or absence of them can help you determine the health of awa or streams in your areas. 

Find out more about Kōtukutuku

Curious critter for January/Kohitātea

Kōtukutuku, or Fuchsia excorticata, is one of Aotearoa New Zealand’s only deciduous trees, meaning the leaves are lost in winter.

Read the full feature story

Taiea te Taiao 

Taiea te Taiao, Maungatautari to Pirongia Ecological Corridor Project, is establishing a natural corridor of native plantings and a collaborative community to support biodiversity between Sanctuary Mountain Maungatautari and Pirongia maunga in the Waikato.

Read on to find out how they will use eDNA to monitor the changes to the ecosystem over the coming four years.  

Find out more about mayflies

Curious critter for July/Hōngongoi

Our curious critter this month is the mayfly – a type of insect found near freshwater all over the world.

Read the full feature story

Putting a STOP to environmental degradation

We visited the Otago Peninsula for a workshop NZ Marine Studies Centre in February. Lala Frazer from Save the Otago Peninsula was there and, to our delight, invited us to visit the area she sampled and see the work they do. 

Find out more about kōura

Curious critter for April/Paengawhāwhā

As the the leaves begin to fall from trees and dew clings to the ground in the early morning, we shine the light on kōura/kēwai. Read on to learn more about this taonga and valued mahinga kai species.

Read the full feature story

Residents band together for a Wellington Stream

Following repeated pollution in their local stream, locals have banded together to provide information and access to the stream for their community, using eDNA in the process.

Find out more about the mānuka moth

Critter of the month for December/Hakihea

The Wai Tuwhera o te Taiao critter of the month for December/Hakihea is the mānuka moth (also known as Declana floccosa, or the forest semilooper moth).

Read on to find out why two scientists spent 42 years studying these moths in their backyard.

Read the full feature article

Te Whenua Tōmuri Trust trains kaitiaki in eDNA sampling

The Trust, through its taiao monitoring project Maru Wai Matara, has so far helped iwi and hapū kaitiaki and school children take 35 eDNA samples from waterways around Taranaki!

 

Learn more about the kaikōmako tree

Critter of the month for October/Whiringa-ā-nuku

The Wai Tuwhera o te Taiao critter of the month for October/Whiringa-ā-nuku is the kaikōmako tree.

Wait a second, that’s not a critter… it’s a plant! But we think for supporting the many critters in their bubbles, kaikōmako deserve a shout out.

Read the full feature story

“Dead muddy ditch” is in fact teeming with life 

The Ōtokia Creek and Marsh Habitat Trust of Brighton, Dunedin, have always known their little creek was special. Using eDNA has given them an opportunity to showcase some of the biodiversity.

Read more about the redfin bully

Critter of the month - July/Hōngongoi

The critter of the month for July/Hōngongoi is Aotearoa New Zealand's most colourful native fish, the redfin bully.

Ngā Kaimanaaki o te Waimapihi / Polhill Protectors focus on stream health

After receiving their eDNA results, Ngā Kaimanaaki o te Waimapihi / Polhill Protectors have increased their focus on stream health, exploring the biodiversity, history and whakapapa of a stream that flows beneath Wellington City.

 

Read the full feature story

Critter of the month – June / Pipiri

This month, the pouched lamprey / kanakana / piharau (Geotria australis) is crowned critter of the month. 

The DNA of this elusive and ancient migratory fish was found in a wetland area on the West Coast by the Ōkārito Community Association.

Read more about pouched lamprey / kanakana / piharau

Kids restore the Kepler, and discover a rare species in the process

When Fiordland College Year 10 students used eDNA in their ongoing stream comparison study, they were not expecting to find a previously unrecorded species lurking in the stream.

Read the full feature story

Critter of the month  - May / Haratua

This month’s critter is Archichauliodes diversus (puene), the New Zealand dobsonfly.

Learn more about the New Zealand dobsonfly / puene
